newsitem.title: FRANCE: EC plans new European investment fund directive.
newsitem.headline: EC plans new European investment fund directive.

text.p: The European Commission has made new proposals on regulating the European investment fund industry following the recent failure to reach agreement on a directive intended to build on legislation introduced in 1985.

Steffen Matthias, secretary general of the European Federation of Investment Funds and Companies (FEFSI), told a fund management conference the commission failed to reach a compromise on the UCITS 2 directive last month.
The first UCITS directive was introduced in 1985 to improve regulation, standardise products, ensure investor protection and promote cross-border marketing of funds within Europe.
He said the commission had proposed a new scheme that regulates the service provider rather than the product. The original 1985 directive will remain in place.
He said the proposals would seek to "harmonise the authorisation and operating conditions of management companies". It would provide a marketing "passport" to fund managers rather than to a product.
"This is a rather dramatically new idea," he said.
But Matthias told Reuters that the proposals were still at a preliminary stage and were open to debate.

He said the new proposals raised many questions, including how national regulators would react to the scheme, how to operate with two different directives, how the passport for fund managers would work, and how to regulate the fund manager without regulating the product.
He said the decision to retain the 1985 UCITS directive was due to the high number of funds already operating under this regime.
"The commission said that we have thousands and thousands of funds under the 1985 UCITS directive and that we cannot simply withdraw or drop the directive."
Whatever solution was found, he said it was important to preserve the integrity of the industry, protect investors, avoid conflicts of interest and preserve the quality of the UCITS label.
